bull_case: VAS and tokenization increase the amount of value captured per credential and transaction.
bear_case: Regulatory forced-routing and low-cost account-to-account payments can commoditize some domestic debit economics.
thesis: Visa's moat remains exceptionally wide and is still broadening from card rails into services, risk/security and money movement. Alternative rails are real, but Visa often sits as an enabling layer rather than being displaced outright.

evidence.claim: FY2025 payments volume $13.894T and processed transactions 257.545B.
Q3 processed transactions +10% and VAS revenue +33%.

counterevidence: Regulatory and interchange litigation can pressure network economics and pricing over time.
The current valuation already embeds a high-quality compounder profile.
unknowns: Long-run regulation of interchange and routing
Sustainable growth rate of Visa Direct and value-added services
falsifiers: If processed transactions and payments volume decelerate materially while client incentives rise faster than gross revenue, the moat/FCF thesis weakens.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current volume, transaction and VAS growth do not support a persistent shrinking-moat predicate.

next_checks: Payments volume, cross-border volume, processed transactions, value-added services, client incentives, owner FCF/share, buyback price

subscores.rationale: Global acceptance, issuer/acquirer integration, tokenization and brand trust create high switching/friction costs.
Multi-trillion-dollar volume, hundreds of billions of transactions and continuing growth provide measurable network effects plus concrete integration switching costs.
VAS, risk/security, tokenization and money movement add defense layers beyond basic card routing.

uncertainties.rationale: Regulation, incentives and valuation are the main uncertainty.
